triggers: a transformer block built from per-op graph launches needs 1.5x+
elementwise chains between quantized matmuls dominate launch and memory overhead

payload.goal: Collapse a whole transformer block into one mlx lazy graph.

problem.statement: Per-op execution (each op = own graph launch + fp16 memory round-trip) leaves a transformer block 2x+ above the mlx lazy-graph composition.

payload.what: fast::rms_norm + quantized_matmul + fast::scaled_dot_product_attention + mlx elementwise (silu/mul/add) composed as one lazy graph keeps the residual resident in mlx and removes all per-op launches/round-trips. Measured m1024 q4 transformer block: 58.8 ms per-op -> 26.9 ms fused (2.17x); fused time equals the four quantized_matmul kernel times (~24 ms) - at kernel-SOTA parity the fusion overhead is amortized to zero.
payload.when: Any mlx C++ pipeline where blocks are assembled op-by-op through separate graph launches.
payload.how: 1. Compose the block as a function array->array with no evals inside. 2. Keep residual activations as mlx arrays across blocks; read back only at sequence boundaries. 3. Elementwise chains between matmuls fuse automatically; use fast::rms_norm/fast::sdpa rather than hand-composed softmax. 4. Validate stage-by-stage against fp32 references before trusting the fused path.
caveats: mlx fast::sdpa contract is (B, heads, seq, dim) - torch-style; the (B,seq,heads,dim) reading silently computes attention over the wrong axis
fp16 synthetic-data validation diverges on unnormalized weights; normalize scales by 1/sqrt(k) before comparing eval granularities

raw.seed: onyx-infer kernel-agent episode E13, stage-verified vs fp32 references on Apple M5 Max, 2026-11-18

metrics.source: comparable medians, onyx-infer E13, M5 Max: per-op 58.8 ms vs fused 26.9 ms per block
metrics.note: latency-reduction percentage of the fused lazy graph versus the per-op composition
